newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices end flat to down 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices end flat to down 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended even to down 1/8 point Tuesday amid mostly firm new issue pricing, market sources said.
Pricing was especially firm on Georgia and Utah's competitive deals, which one analyst said came "right on the money."

The secondary market saw light action, the analyst said, with high-grade issues ending unchanged. Dollar bonds opened down 1/8 point, then edged up to be just a few basis points weaker by noon (EDT), but faded to close down 1/8 point, he said.
A trader said while he saw some business in the intermediate range, the long end was quiet.
"We saw some selling early today but we're really not hearing of any going away business, which is kind of frustrating," he said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 5/32 at 101-24/32 to yield 6.49 percent at close to 1700 EDT. In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed down 1/32 at 120-13/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 2/32 at 114-19/32. The MOB spread was 186 ticks.
Turning to new issues, PaineWebber Inc repriced $289 million New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority bonds, raising the top yield in 2021 to 5.50 percent from 5.474 percent.
Tom Moles, a managing director at J&W Seligman, passed on the deal.

"I am not going to be a participant because I own some of the older bonds which have great coupons compared to what they are coming to the market with. I think it will probably get done though," Moles said.
The deal was priced about where he expected given where the overall market was, Moles said.
"(It was) a little bit poor timing on their part that they came right when we had a little hiccup in the marketplace," he said. "From an investor's standpoint it's probably an opportunity."

On the competitive side, JP Morgan Securities won the $240 million Georgia bonds at a net interest cost of 4.7584 percent. The sale went off at 1100 EDT and JP Morgan reported the account closed by 1220 EDT. The deal is rated triple-A by Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's Corp and Fitch Investors Service.

Weyman Smith, director of the Georgia State Financing Commission, said he was "very pleased" with the offering. While aware of the hit bond prices took Friday after strong news on employment and manufacturing, Smith said the selloff was not cause for grave concern. Rates are still relatively low, he said.

"We obviously thought about what happened on Friday, and Monday we came in and looked at where the triple-A levels were," Smith said. "I mean they were backed off a little bit, but it still wasn't significant."
The director believes the deal's non-callable structure, which the state has had in place for several years, also saved some money in borrowing costs.
"That's a rate call I think, at least in my opinion," he said.

Should rates rise to a point where Georgia believes a better chance exists for rates to go down enough to obtain a reasonable savings in a refunding, the state would re-instate a call feature, Smith said.
"But I think that rate is somewhere a little in excess of a six percent that would lead us to do that anyway," he said.

In addition to being non-callable, the couponing on the Georgia deal was interesting, a municipal analyst said. He also cited a $205 millon Utah general obligation deal that Lehman Brothers won at a 4.7692 percent true interest cost.
"The unique thing about the Utahs is that they are callable at par," he said.
Back on the negotiated side, Smith Barney Inc restructured $227 million Austin, Texas, combined utility systems revenue refunding bonds. The top yield, however, remained 5.43 percent in 2020.

Goldman Sachs & Co repriced $115 million New York State Environmental Facilities Corp bonds, raising yields in several maturities. The top yield in 2019 was raised to 5.42 percent from 5.38 percent. Goldman also restructured the deal, eliminating the 2014 maturity.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
